Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Luminous, rich colours; crisp focal details on the face and costume, softer painted edges toward the distance.
Face proportions: a short midface and a soft, gently rounded jawline with a small soft chin; any crown or headpiece sits above her hairline. Her eyes keep the shape and size described below.

Face — her own: a cheerful, sunny openness; fair skin; heart-shaped face; large eyes — wide almond eyes, outer eye corners slightly lifted; soft rounded brows; small button nose; small bow lips; magenta eyes; rosy flushed cheeks.

Expression: a light teasing smile, bright eyes.
Her element, carried in her design: ruthenium: a hard, brittle silver-white metal of the platinum family, the last of its six sisters to be found, isolated in 1844 at Kazan University from the stubborn residue of Ural platinum ore and named for Ruthenia, the old Latin name of Russia; a little of it makes platinum harder, and with osmium and iridium it forms the tiny hard bead at the tip of a fountain-pen nib that lasts decades of writing; its catalysts swap partners between molecules and join them anew, and its wine-red dyes colour glass that turns sunlight into electricity.

No crown unless the opening line says she wears one; steam, pipes and gauges in the scene.
Silhouette: a long tailcoat over a waistcoat, a small silk top hat and a pocket-watch chain — a gentleman inventor's upright shape. Only the overall shape is fixed; design the details freely in the element's materials and palette. This silhouette overrides the overall shape of the costume above.

Pose: standing confidently, her body turned slightly while her face looks toward the viewer.
Light: bright warm sunlight with soft sky light bounced from white clouds.
Composition: vertical 2:3 full-body framing with modest headroom and clear space below the boots — the whole figure from the top of her head or headpiece to both feet stays inside the frame, occupying about four-fifths of the image height, with the same camera distance in every world; her hands stay inside the frame. Camera level with her face with natural portrait perspective; her head level, chin neither raised nor tucked — no upward perspective on her face, no wide-angle distortion, no low angle, no close crop.

One figure only; no text or numbers except her element's own chemical symbol (Ru) and atomic number (44) — and those only as part of the scene: engraved, embroidered or glowing on her costume, a banner, a sign or a machine, never as a floating label, corner badge, periodic-table tile, caption or overlay on the picture; no logo or watermark.
